name: Hilarius Pictaviensis
pdTranslations: De Trinitate (books i–xii) and select Homilies on Psalms I, LIII, CXXX in NPNF Series 2, Volume 9 (1886–1900), translated by E.W. Watson and others. First English translation of any Hilary works.
modernTranslations: NPNF is public domain (19th-c.); no major modern copyrighted translations noted.
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary on the Psalms and numerous other homilies remain untranslated; incomplete coverage of De Trinitate (books xiii+ not in NPNF).

name: Alexander III (Pope)
pdTranslations: None identified; no ANF/NPNF coverage of his writings.
modernTranslations: Boso's Life of Alexander III translated by G.M. Ellis (Rowman & Littlefield, 1973). Some letters referenced in scholarship but no full translation project identified.
untranslatedHighlights: Papal correspondence (Epistolae), Sententiae Rolandi (canonical work), anti-Islamic polemics remain untranslated or inaccessible in modern English.

name: Joannes Saresberiensis (John of Salisbury)
pdTranslations: None in ANF/NPNF; however, older translations exist: Metalogicon by Daniel McGarry (UC Press, 1955, first modern-language translation); Policraticus ('Frivolities of Courtiers') by J.B. Pike (University of Minnesota Press, 1938).
modernTranslations: Metalogicon by J.B. Hall (Corpus Christianorum in Translation 12, 2013); Policraticus by C.J. Nederman (Cambridge, 1990). Both major works now available in modern scholarly editions.
untranslatedHighlights: Letters and minor treatises have limited coverage; some correspondence remains inaccessible in English.

name: Smaragdus S. Michaelis
modernTranslations: Diadema Monachorum and Commentary on the Rule of St. Benedict translated by David Barry (Cistercian Studies Series). This is a significant Carolingian monastic commentary.
untranslatedHighlights: Most other works (homilies, various treatises) remain in Latin; comprehensive corpus incomplete in English.

name: Remigius Antissiodorensis
modernTranslations: No modern English translations identified. Works exist only in Latin manuscripts and scholarly editions.
untranslatedHighlights: Extensive glosses and commentaries on classical texts (Vergil, Terence, Cato), biblical commentaries (Genesis, Psalms), and works on Boethius, Martianus Capella, and grammarians—all untranslated.

name: Auctor incertus (Hieronymus Stridonensis?)
pdTranslations: Unknown; uncertain/disputed attribution, possibly tentatively attributed to Jerome (Hieronymus Stridonensis) but marked with uncertainty in PL database.
modernTranslations: Status unknown due to attribution uncertainty. Cannot determine translation coverage when authorship is unresolved.
untranslatedHighlights: Uncertain identity prevents assessment; historical scholarship may contest whether this corpus exists or merits translation.

name: Joannes Scotus Erigena
modernTranslations: Periphyseon (De Divisione Naturae): Complete translation by I.P. Sheldon-Williams and John J. O'Meara (Dumbarton Oaks, 1987); Partial translation by Myra Uhlfelder (1976, Yale, covers ~half, Book 1 complete); Critical edition with translation by Édouard Jeauneau (Books 1–5, 1996–2003). Major medieval philosophical work well represented.
untranslatedHighlights: Some minor works and commentaries on pseudo-Dionysius remain partially inaccessible in English.

name: Petrus Blesensis
modernTranslations: Letters: G.A. Loud has translated some letters concerning Sicily; contributions to Ingulph's Chronicle continuation translated by Henry T. Riley. Limited corpus available.
untranslatedHighlights: Majority of correspondence, sermons in allegorical style, commentaries on Scripture, treatises, and polemics against clergy and Jews remain untranslated.

name: Petrus Cluniacensis (Peter the Venerable)
modernTranslations: No comprehensive English translation of his theological writings located. Peter commissioned translations of Islamic texts (Qur'an, al-Kindi Apology, Islamic law summaries) into Latin (completed 1143, published 1543 by Bibliander), but his own works remain largely untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Monastic writings, theological treatises, anti-Jewish and anti-Islamic polemics, letters—vast corpus remains in Latin.

name: Guibertus S. Mariae de Novigento (Guibert of Nogent)
modernTranslations: Gesta Dei per Francos (Deeds of God through the Franks): translated by Robert Levine. De vita sua (Autobiography/Memoirs, 'Monodiae', 1115): also available in English. Important First Crusade source.
untranslatedHighlights: Other theological treatises, hagiographic works, and some correspondence remain untranslated.

name: Anselmus Cantuariensis (St. Anselm)
pdTranslations: Works of St. Anselm by Sidney Norton Deane (1903, public domain): includes Proslogium, Monologium, Cur Deus Homo, and philosophical essays. Remains widely available.
modernTranslations: Letters of Saint Anselm translated by Walter Fröhlich (1990–1994). Anselm of Canterbury: The Major Works edited by Brian Davies and others (Oxford, 1998). Complete Philosophical and Theological Treatises by Jasper Hopkins and Herbert Richardson.
untranslatedHighlights: Some minor prayers, meditations, and occasional treatises have limited modern coverage, but major works well represented.

name: Ordericus Vitalis
modernTranslations: Ecclesiastical History: Complete edition and translation in 6 volumes by Marjorie Chibnall (Oxford Medieval Texts, scholarly series, 1969–). Comprehensive modern English translation with parallel Latin text.
untranslatedHighlights: None; the Historia Ecclesiastica (primary work of significance) is fully translated.

name: Benedictus Nursiae (St. Benedict)
pdTranslations: Rule of St. Benedict: numerous translations including Leonard J. Doyle (Liturgical Press, 2001 reissue), Justin McCann (modified for American English). Historical public-domain translations exist.
modernTranslations: RB 1980: The Rule of St. Benedict in English (Timothy Fry, OSB, ed.); multiple modern scholarly editions (Liturgical Press, Abbey Press, Solesmes). Rule well covered by multiple modern translations.
untranslatedHighlights: Other works and writings attributed to Benedict beyond the Rule have minimal documentation and limited translation; scholarly focus on the Rule dominates.

name: Alanus de Insulis (Alain of Lille)
pdTranslations: De Planctu Naturae (Complaint of Nature): translated by Douglas M. Moffat (Yale Studies in English, v. 36, 1908; reprinted 1972). Public-domain translation available.
modernTranslations: Anticlaudianus and other works have limited modern English coverage; De Planctu Naturae remains best represented.
untranslatedHighlights: Anticlaudianus (didactic philosophical poem), theological treatises, and minor works remain largely untranslated.

name: Tertullianus
pdTranslations: ANF Volumes III–IV (Ante-Nicene Fathers): comprehensive coverage translated by Rev. Peter Holmes and Rev. Sydney Thelwall. ANF III ('Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian') includes Apologetic, Anti-Marcion, and Ethical works; ANF IV continues coverage. Public domain, widely available online.
modernTranslations: FOTC 'Disciplinary, Moral and Ascetical Works' (Vol. 40, 1959) by Rudolphus Arbesmann, Emily Joseph Daly, and Edwin A. Quain. CCEL database shows 33 Tertullian works available in translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Some fragmentary works and rare treatises may remain untranslated; ANF+FOTC together provide substantial but not exhaustive coverage.

name: Petrus Comestor
modernTranslations: Historia Scholastica: Medieval English translations existed (noted in PL records) but no readily accessible modern English translation. Academic translation project underway (multi-volume, mentioned in Brepols catalog) but not yet widely published.
untranslatedHighlights: The Historia Scholastica ('Medieval Popular Bible'), the most significant work, remains largely inaccessible in modern English despite 800+ surviving medieval manuscripts and significant historical influence.

name: Adamus Scotus (Adam of Dryburgh)
modernTranslations: No modern English translations located. Works published in Latin by Aegidius Gourmont (Paris, 1518) and appear in patrological databases, but remain inaccessible in English.
untranslatedHighlights: De tripartito tabernaculo (1180), Liber de quadripartito exercitio cellae, sermons, and theological writings—entire corpus untranslated.

name: Thomas Cisterciensis (Thomas of Perseigne)
modernTranslations: Erudite Commentary on the Song of Songs: French translation by Pierre-Yves Émery (Frère de Taizé, 2011: 'THOMAS LE CISTERCIEN, Commentaire sur le Cantique des Cantiques'). No modern English translation identified.
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary on Song of Songs (the principal surviving work, 78 surviving manuscripts) and other Cistercian writings remain untranslated to English.

name: Atto Vercellensis
modernTranslations: No modern English translations identified. Works (Polypticum on Italian morality, De pressuris ecclesiasticis on ecclesiastical affairs, biblical glosses) remain in Latin manuscripts and scholarly editions only.
untranslatedHighlights: Polypticum, De pressuris ecclesiasticis, biblical commentaries—corpus untranslated.

name: Maurini
pdTranslations: N/A—Maurini refers to Benedictine editors' notes and critical apparatus in Migne's Patrologia Latina (1844–1864), not original author works.
modernTranslations: N/A—This is a collective editorial contribution to Migne's compilation, not a primary textual corpus requiring individual translation.
untranslatedHighlights: N/A—Not applicable to authorial works.
